titleArabic: الشيخ الأكبر محيي الدين ابن عربي

verses.ar:
Name and title: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Muhammad Ibn Arabi al-Ta'i al-Hatimi, known as Muhyiddin (Reviver of the Religion) and al-Shaykh al-Akbar (the Greatest Shaykh).
Born: Ramadan 560 AH (1165 CE), Murcia, al-Andalus. The sources differ on the day (17th or 27th).
Died: 22 Rabi al-Thani 638 AH (November 1240 CE), Damascus; buried on Mount Qasiyun. Sources give 8 or 16 November.
Teachers: many scholars and saints in al-Andalus and North Africa, among them Fatima bint Ibn al-Muthanna of Seville, and al-Uryani, his first master.
Students: Sadr al-Din al-Qunawi, his stepson and chief interpreter, and Ismail ibn Sawdakin.
Works: al-Futuhat al-Makkiyya (begun in Mecca in 598 AH, finished about 635 AH), Fusus al-Hikam (completed in Damascus about 627–628 AH) and the poems Tarjuman al-Ashwaq.

Shaykh Muhyiddin Ibn Arabi (QS) was born in Murcia in 1165 and grew up in Seville, where his family settled after the Almohad takeover of Murcia. He studied the Qur'an, hadith and jurisprudence with many teachers, and as a young man he entered the path of the Sufis, keeping the company of the saints of al-Andalus and North Africa, among them the saintly woman Fatima bint Ibn al-Muthanna of Seville. In 1201 or 1202 he left the West for Mecca and never returned. He travelled through Egypt, Jerusalem, Iraq and Anatolia, and in 620 AH (1223) settled in Damascus, where he taught, wrote and received seekers until he passed away on 22 Rabi al-Thani 638 AH. He is buried on Mount Qasiyun, and his urs is kept on that day.

Ibn Arabi wrote some hundreds of works on the knowledge of Allah, the inner reality of the Prophet ﷺ, the stations of the saints and the unseen. In the Futuhat al-Makkiyya, begun beside the Ka'ba, he shows the whole of the religion, its acts of worship and the spiritual states that grow from them, as a path to knowing Allah; the Fusus al-Hikam takes each prophet as a wisdom of the Divine Names. His followers called him al-Shaykh al-Akbar, the Greatest Shaykh, and his stepson Sadr al-Din al-Qunawi (QS) began the work of explaining and passing on his teachings. For the people of the path he stands among the great knowers of Allah and the masters of the secrets of the heart, and his books are read in the circles of the Sufis, under the guidance of a shaykh, as a key to the realities behind the sacred law, which he held to be the root of every station.
